clue.text: Fruit returned — half a pound

indicators.note: returned means the whole run of letters built from the next words is read backwards

parts.note: semi- is the prefix meaning half
L (libra) is the abbreviation for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Some fruit has been sent back, and only half a pound of it at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns SEMI + L, giving LIMES; 'a pound' is one piece, the single letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: Small green citrus fruits are limes.

clue.text: Tall fellow takes Mr French in to racecourse

parts.note: long means tall

indicators.note: takes means the fellow's letters take in, contain, the next piece

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
M is short for monsieur, the French Mr

explanation.surface: A tall man takes a Frenchman to the races.
explanation.walkthrough: Longchamp is the Paris racecourse, home of the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse-racing track in the Bois de Boulogne in Paris is Longchamp.

clue.text: Cut in fashion, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the word for fashion is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: mode means fashion, as in a la mode

explanation.surface: A cut that is said to be fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a haircut; it is the lawn cut, past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass that has been mowed has been cut.

clue.text: Cricketer in casual wear — appears on edge

indicators.note: in a down clue, appears on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: shorts are casual clothing
a lip is an edge or rim

explanation.surface: A cricketer in shorts turns up at the boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: Short slip is a fielding position close behind the batter in cricket, the bat-and-ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: A fielder placed close behind the wicket, near the slips, is named after that position.

clue.text: Dickensian with capacity to express contempt

parts.note: a peck is an old dry measure of capacity, a quarter of a bushel
to sniff is to show disdain with a scornful intake of breath

explanation.surface: A Dickens character is described as able to show scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: Seth Pecksniff is the oily hypocrite in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a character created by Charles Dickens in Martin Chuzzlewit.

clue.text: Little fish cake?

parts.note: read as a baby pike, really a small thick griddle cake like a crumpet

explanation.surface: A small fishcake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little fish' suggests the diminutive of pike; the word names a small griddle cake in British and Australian use.
explanation.definitionFit: A small thick pancake or crumpet in Britain and Australia is called by this name, which also looks like a young pike.

clue.text: Accountant joins French composer in ship

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
Maurice Ravel was the French composer of Bolero

explanation.surface: An accountant and a French musician are aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravel is a small sailing vessel of the 15th and 16th centuries.

clue.text: Promise to give direction on river

parts.note: S is south, a compass direction
the Wear is a river in northeast England through Durham

explanation.surface: A vow to give someone directions to the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places S above the river in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to vow or pledge solemnly.

clue.text: One flower in ten perhaps is undamaged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in puts the flower letters inside the rearranged number
perhaps hints that the number word may take a different form, so its letters are reshuffled

parts.note: a viola is a flower of the violet family

explanation.surface: One flower among ten may be unspoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns TEN into N...TE, which holds VIOLA, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left unbroken and unharmed is intact, free from violation.

clue.text: Loud complaint about Roundhead in ruffle

parts.note: F is forte, musical for loud
the head of Round, its first letter
an illness is a complaint, so ill fits

explanation.surface: A noisy objection to a Cromwellian soldier wearing a ruffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roundhead' suggests a Puritan soldier of the English Civil War; it gives the head of 'Round', R.
explanation.definitionFit: A frill is a decorative ruffle of gathered fabric.

clue.text: Well-read US citizen?

parts.note: a resident of a big American city, who is also a widely read weekly magazine of that name

explanation.surface: An American who reads a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-read' is not about the citizen's learning: the magazine itself is the thing widely read.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a famous weekly magazine is also the term for someone living in America's largest city.

clue.text: Last words — I've no need of doctoring!

indicators.note: something in need of doctoring must be tampered with, so the letters before it are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's dying words declare they have no use for a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need of doctoring' rearranges IVENO (from I've and no) into the answer; the surface makes doctoring medical.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoi is the short closing stanza of a poem, its final lines.

clue.text: Retired journalist has whip-round for trainee

indicators.note: round says the whip's letters go around the other piece

parts.note: a cat (cat-o'-nine-tails) is a whip

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going back, so the journalist's letters run backwards

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A retired reporter is given a collection from colleagues, for a trainee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whip-round' looks like a collection of money; split it so 'round' puts CAT around DE (ED with 'Retired' turning it).
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young person in training for the armed forces or police.

clue.text: City supplies meat and game

parts.note: liver is offal eaten as meat
pool is a cue game played on a table

explanation.surface: A city provides food and sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool is a major port city in northwest England.

clue.text: A bearer of ermine, about fifty, in Elaine's home

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the animal's letters go round the next piece

parts.note: the stoat's white winter coat is ermine
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An ermine-clad figure aged about fifty is at Elaine's house.
explanation.walkthrough: In Arthurian legend and Tennyson, Elaine is the Lily Maid of Astolat; 'bearer of ermine' reads like a noble in robes but is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaine of Astolat is the Arthurian maiden whose town gives her title.

clue.text: Kind lift to German poet in Scottish beauty spot

indicators.note: in a down clue, lift raises the letters so they read upwards, backwards

parts.note: sort means kind
Hans Sachs was a German poet and Meistersinger

explanation.surface: A friendly ride offered to a German poet in a lovely Scottish spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind lift' reads as a friendly car ride; 'lift' turns SORT into TROS. The Trossachs is a wooded glen area in Stirlingshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trossachs is a celebrated scenic area of lochs and hills in central Scotland.

clue.text: Thirsty European region?

parts.note: playfully read as a country where everyone laps up drink, really the Arctic region of northern Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A dry corner of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue splits the name into a land that laps, as a thirsty animal does.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern Scandinavian area home to the Sami is a European region, and lapping is how a thirsty dog drinks.

clue.text: Turn in prices for customs

indicators.note: in places the turn letters inside the word prices

parts.note: an act is a turn on stage

explanation.surface: A change in prices at customs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'customs' suggests border officials; it means habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Customs are habitual ways of doing things, established usages.

clue.text: Scattered Red spies at Land's End

definitions.text: Scattered Red spies at Land's End

indicators.note: scattered means flung about, so the letters of the spies are mixed
End picks the last letter of Land's

explanation.surface: Communist agents have fled in all directions in far Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scattered' rearranges REDSPIES into DISPERSE, then 'End' adds D, the last letter of 'Land's'; the whole clue describes spies dispersed. Land's End is England's southwest tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Spies sent off in every direction have been spread widely.

clue.text: Actors' reminders for training in writing

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: in places the training letters inside the writing letters

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: Notes help actors to train in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines whispered from the wings to an actor who has forgotten them are prompts.

clue.text: Point to TV ratings in a show of endurance

parts.note: S is south, a compass point
TAM, Television Audience Measurement, was the old British TV ratings system
taken as written

explanation.surface: Viewing figures suggest a programme of stamina.
explanation.walkthrough: TAM was the British television audience measurement of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, what a show of endurance demonstrates.

clue.text: Some of them charge for their work

definitions.text: Some of them charge for their work

parts.words: Some of them charge for their work
parts.note: charge here means fill a gun with powder and shot, the job of an assistant to a shooter, not ask a fee

explanation.surface: Some workers bill for their services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests fees; it means filling a gun, as a shooting party's assistant does.
explanation.definitionFit: At a shoot, assistants who fill the guns for the shooters do their work by charging them.

clue.text: Displays view of fells

definitions.meaning: arranges for show, as goods in a shop
fells read as knocks down, a boxer's view of what flooring an opponent does

explanation.surface: A display of the Lake District hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fells' looks like the noun for northern English hills; read it as a verb, to knock someone down.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out goods for show, and to knock someone flat, share the phrase.

clue.text: Accountant's so cautious a bird

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant, plus the possessive S
wary means cautious

explanation.surface: An accountant is said to be a very careful creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The cassowary is a large flightless bird of New Guinea and Australia.

clue.text: Hide large surplus?

definitions.meaning: in finance, the margin by which earnings exceed a payment, a big excess

explanation.surface: Concealing a big excess.
explanation.walkthrough: Dividend cover is the ratio of profit to dividend paid, a surplus margin.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen something conceals it, and in accounts it names the excess of profit over dividend.

clue.text: Horrible creatures, some progressive types ?

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words, so the letters are found within them

explanation.surface: Some forward-looking people are monsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are hideous man-eating giants of folklore.

clue.text: Scottish striker .collects waste materials

indicators.note: materials is read as the word materialising in a new arrangement, so the letters before it are reworked

explanation.surface: A Scottish footballer gathers up scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' suggests a footballer; a tawse is the leather strap once used to beat Scottish schoolchildren.
explanation.definitionFit: The leather strap formerly used for corporal punishment in Scottish schools strikes the hand.

clue.text: All 7?

definitions.meaning: the answer to 7 down, meaning undamaged or intact

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is another clue's answer, INVIOLATE at 7, meaning unbroken.
explanation.definitionFit: The entire amount is the sum, and something intact is unbroken, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Service leader against one Corps retreating

parts.note: V stands for versus, against
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the corps letters run backwards

parts.note: RAC is the Royal Armoured Corps

explanation.surface: A soldier's leader opposes one corps that is falling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' is a church service, not the armed services the rest of the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish priest leads a church service.

clue.text: Club takes peevish view of decoration

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
taking a cross view is being peevish and annoyed

explanation.surface: A club member is irritated by someone's attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: The German military medal for bravery is a famous decoration.

clue.text: Opposed to manufacturing train sets

indicators.note: manufacturing means making something new, so the letters of the toy set are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone objects to making model railways.
explanation.definitionFit: Something opposed to a force withstands it, as in heat-resistant.

clue.text: There's a low one in Imphal

definitions.text: There's a low one in Imphal

parts.words: There's a low one in Imphal
parts.note: the Indian town's name contains the letters for miles per hour, a unit of how fast, and a low one is sitting there

explanation.surface: An Indian town has a modest limit.
explanation.walkthrough: Imphal is a city in northeast India; its middle letters MPH are the measure of velocity.
explanation.definitionFit: Miles per hour measures how fast something goes, and its letters sit inside the town's name.
